title: Art direction
author: Quiet-Phase6948
selftext:
So I have no issues with AI help when it comes to code, certain tasks are just made easier, such as a random map generation, AI behaviour etc. 

  
But AI art assets, will almost always look terrible, especially if you use the ChatGPT/NanoBanana image generation, it is absolutely terrible. Please stop using it. There are plenty of free placeholder assets on [itch.io](http://itch.io), or even reasonably paid assets you can use. Art direction is one of the most important things of a game, and it is one of those things AI can never understand, it might write code well, but it cannot understand visuals, the aesthetics you are going for, so please, stop.

comments.author: AdStreet4350
comments.body: Do you have any examples? Honestly, AI can create great sprite assets; you just have to retouch them

replies.author: Quiet-Phase6948
replies.body: Not at the top of my head, it is just what I see when I scroll through. Some really great ideas out there that are let down by people just not caring about the graphical assets, now, I understand it might be placeholders, I am just venting a bit.

comments.author: Aggressive_Tie_3014
comments.body:
Yeah, AI code assistance is exactly what this kind of technology excels in and what I always assumed it would be. Speeding up tedious technical work, and giving you solutions to technical problems. It is a total game changer and just fantastic.

AI-generated imagery, writing and audio though is always missing something that so far only a human touch can give it. A kind of boring uncanny valley that's always there as a result of being the average of billions of images, words or songs I guess.

replies.author: Quiet-Phase6948
replies.body: I agree, and it all kind of looks the same. Granted this is a problem AAA studios have as well with human created assets, so it is not unique to AI, but I think indie games can do better.

comments.author: davesoft
comments.body: Folks will do as they please.

comments.author: kkreinn
comments.body: A mi no me importaría hacer el arte en mi propio juego, pero programar es lo más complicado, exigente y tedioso que existe.

replies.author: Quiet-Phase6948
replies.body: For programming AI works really well, as it is clearly defined, there is very little that stops you from using AI to create the systems and logic.

replies.author: kkreinn
replies.body: Si tienes nociones de programación y sabes lo que haces, sí, pero por lo que tengo visto la IA no es buena en proyectos largos. Es buena si hace un juego corto ella sola o hace de revisor o creador de trozos de código que te puedan ayudar, pero ya está, no es la gran cosa como la venden. He visto a gente intentar programar en Fable y no ha dado buenos resultados.

comments.author: Sneezy_23
comments.body: Ai art assets are a bad idea.

comments.author: lyeeedar
comments.body:
Yes I agree. Use local ai (flux, illustrious, etc) and Loras to ensure you make an art style, then use the big models to edit or guide. Use controlnet to set composition, multiple levels of denoises to correct issues, and can editing to stitch parts from images together.

The issue is never ai. It's LOW EFFORT ai.

replies.author: Quiet-Phase6948
replies.body: Fair, custom trained LORAs would give a coherent art direction, but you are still very much relying on the art direction of others for the checkpoints.
